To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the average number of articles per author in leading management journals increased by 39.4% between 1967 and 1992.
there has been a significant increase in the number of authors of articles in leading management journals over a 25-year period and that this increase varied across the journals studied.
the average number of articles per issue in the eight journals studied increased from 1.3 to 1.9 over a 25-yr. period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an important trend in academic publishing, the increasing number of authors per research paper. We believe this trend is
an important aspect of the psychology of the scientist, i.e., the authorship of scientific articles.
an important aspect of the socialization of scientists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increase in the number of authors on articles in leading management journals has occurred because of the increasing complexity of research and the need for more authors to be involved in research.
the increase in the number of authors on an article in the leading management journals has been substantial and significant over the last quarter of a century.
there has been a dramatic increase in the number of authors in articles published in the eight leading management journals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a significant increase in the number of authors on management research articles, and that this increase is not due solely to the number of co-authors on articles, but also to the increase of multiple co-authors on a single article.
the average number of articles per issue increased, the number of pages per issue increased, and the number of articles per page decreased.
the number of authors on articles in leading management journals has been increasing, but the rate of increase varies by journal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of authors on articles is increasing, and that there may be several factors contributing to this increase.
the average number of coauthors on a paper has risen dramatically in the last 30 years, and this is a trend that shows no signs of slowing down.

there is a significant increase in the number of authors of articles in the eight leading journals in management over the past 26 years, with the number increasing from 1.3 in 1967–1971 to 1.9 in 1987–1991, a 39% increase.
